data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement the gov-copy-writer sub-agent (model: sonnet) that reads an epic's Copy Needs section, loads top-K (K ≤ 20) federal-style-canon entries via ref-query.sh, applies the documented precedence ladder, and emits a YAML artifact conforming to the gov-copy-artifact schema.
**Why**: Without the agent, no copy artifact is produced; this is the central producer that turns Copy Needs into structured plain-language copy.
**Scope**:
- IN: agent file with prompt; canon retrieval via ref-query.sh with K ≤ 20 cap; precedence ladder application; structured rationale emission (rule_ids, conflicts, deviations); artifact write at configured copy_dir
- OUT: `checks` block computation (separate story — deterministic post-processor); coordination-pass logic (separate story); canon entry authoring (separate story)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, dispatching gov-copy-writer with a sample Copy Needs section produces a YAML file at the configured copy_dir that passes the gov-copy-artifact YAML validator
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, each item in the produced artifact carries values.label, values.hint, values.errors, and a rationale block with non-empty rule_ids citing canon entries returned by ref-query.sh
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, when two canon rules conflict on the same item, the agent records the conflict in rationale.conflicts and selects per the documented precedence ladder
  ← Satisfies: sc-6
- When this story is complete, the agent prompt documents the precedence ladder verbatim and the top-K cap (K ≤ 20) on canon entries loaded per dispatch
  ← Satisfies: sc-6
- When this story is complete, the agent does not populate the `checks` block (leaves the fields null or unset) so the deterministic post-processor owns those values exclusively
  ← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, when the agent produces an item it expects to fail an sc-7 threshold (fk_grade > 8, contains a banned word, or passive voice), it populates rationale.deviations[] with {rule_id, reason} at authoring time, where the reason field is authored by the LLM and is not synthesized by deterministic post-processing
  ← Satisfies: sc-7 (sc-7: "items below threshold are flagged in rationale.deviations with documented reason")
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations
- [Determinism] Forbid agent self-attestation of fk_grade / banned_words / active_voice in the agent prompt; test asserts the agent leaves these unset.
- [Token budget] K ≤ 20 cap protects the agent's context against large canon corpora.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a sprint orchestrator, I have a gov-copy-writer sub-agent that emits a schema-conforming artifact from Copy Needs
